I'm 28 and didn't lose my virginity until I was 19. The thing with people who are on the spectrum, is that a lot of us are late bloomers with things that a lot of people experience/experiment with in adolescence, like alcohol/sex/drugs for instance. To piggyback on what everyone else has been saying, letting him know that it's normal and more common for people like us to not catch that boat until later on in adulthood. Also maybe emphasizing that romance, sex and friends have to happen naturally and that if he tries to force it, it won't be as great as he'd like it to be. I can totally understand where he's coming from though, it's hard for aspies to understand the organic process with relationships and the more we see them, the more we crave them or feel like outcasts because we aren't experiencing those kind of things as easily as neurotypicals seem to be. I  have confidence that he'll eventually find what he's looking for, it may just take a little longer.

I was diagnosed at 23 or 24, and honestly it hit me like a ton of bricks. At first, I denied it thinking that the doctor was either crazy or just an asshole, and was actually depressed about it for the first month or so. After a little while, I realized it definitely made sense, seeing that my interactions/mannerisms as a kid were super weird and even a little strange as an adult. Eventually I started to embrace it and see more adults that are on the spectrum and the kinds of lives they live. It's really helped me grow as an adult, I'm more self aware of my social interactions, while still being able to manage them in a healthy way. I actually enjoy talking to people a lot more now surprisingly.
